claim: Prompted self-correction without external feedback does not improve, and often lowers, LLM reasoning accuracy (CommonSenseQA GPT-3.5 75.8 to 38.1 after one round; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0 after two). So an assumption-check step that only asks the model to re-look at its own answer is not a safe gain. Update: SCoRe base model on MATH 52.6 to 41.4, with 15.8% of items going correct to incorrect vs 4.6% fixed; the blind spot is 64.5% (Sonnet 4 non-reasoning 41.4%) and 'Wait' or an external-voice frame removes much of it; reasoning models show little blind spot.
agent_test: Equal-token arms: plain answer vs self-check vs self-check with external verifier; count correct-to-incorrect flips.

claim: Multi-agent debate beats single answers in the original studies (Du: arithmetic 67.0 to 81.8, GSM8K 77.0 to 85.0; Liang counter-intuitive AR 26.0 to 37.0 on GPT-3.5).
agent_test: Replicate at equal tokens against self-consistency.

claim: At equal compute, debate does not beat self-consistency or ensembling: GSM8K 9 responses SC 88.2 vs debate 83.0; Medprompt beats debate protocols and is cheaper; only ~15% of 36 configs show significant wins over CoT.
agent_test: Always compare any devil's-advocate arm with majority vote over the same number of samples.

claim: Debate and devil's-advocate gains depend on tuning disagreement intensity; forcing disagreement on everything is not best and the best level differs by task (counter-intuitive tasks gain, MedQA does not). Multi-Persona moves from worst to best with 90% agreement prompt.
agent_test: Sweep adversary strength on two task types; pick by validation.

claim: Debate or heterogeneous model mixes help more than same-model debate (Heter-SoM +6.4% over SoM average). Contested: Self-MoA (Li 2025) finds repeated samples from the single best model beat mixing models (+6.6% AlpacaEval 2.0, +3.8% average) because mixing lowers proposer quality.
agent_test: Compare same-model vs mixed-model rivals at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs are sycophantic: asking 'Are you sure?' cuts accuracy up to 27%, models flip first answers 32-86% of the time, and a user-suggested wrong answer cuts accuracy up to 27%. A devil's-advocate or challenge step can induce wrong flips. Update: debate among small models lowered group accuracy over rounds and correct-to-incorrect flips exceeded fixes; a correctness payoff in the prompt did not reduce flips (Wynn 2025).
agent_test: Challenge correct answers and measure flip rate; keep an answer-hold rule.

claim: Biasing features in the prompt cut accuracy up to 36% on BIG-Bench Hard and chain-of-thought explanations do not reveal them; stated reasoning is not proof that assumptions were checked.
agent_test: Insert a biasing hint and test whether the assumption list mentions it.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Humans: Task layout changes evidence use. In students (N=161) the row layout gave 60.8% balanced choices vs 38.2% for the column (ACH-style) layout and 32.7% for paragraph; 56.5% overall used confirming-only; analysts 66.1% balanced.
agent_test: Not directly testable; test structured table vs paragraph rival layout in the agent.

claim: ACH training gives no reliable gain in accuracy or ratings: analysts N=50 no accuracy gain; law students N=191 no guilt-rating difference; experts N=159 ACH effect F(1,153)=1.79, p=.183.
agent_test: Compare agent with and without an explicit hypothesis matrix on a diagnostic evidence task at equal tokens.

claim: Real-world SAT use is sparse and effect evidence thin: of sampled CIA assessments 23 showed no SAT use and 6 extensive use; experiments by Folker (one large gain, one near zero) and Mitre show effects only in some groups; NIC 10 of 14 no explicit SAT.
agent_test: Treat SAT lore as a prior, not proof.

claim: Content analysis of 138 simulation reports: SAT use correlates only weakly with accuracy and slightly with norm adherence (probability ranges, timelines, number of techniques).
agent_test: Test probability-range standardisation as a cheap output rule.

claim: Mandel & Karvetski 2020 (N=227, graffiti task, two hypotheses): ACH was marginally less reliable than control, showed pseudo-diagnosticity, and gave no gain in coherence, consistency or conservatism. Wilcox & Mandel 2024 tally of 6 experiments: ACH never improved accuracy (MAE), improved confirmation bias only in non-analysts (Lehner 2008), and was worse on reliability, diagnosticity (2 studies), and base-rate use; no pooled effect size was computed.
agent_test: Check coherence of the agent's hypothesis probabilities summing to 1.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: LLM idea generation can beat humans on rated novelty (human 4.84, AI 5.64, AI plus rerank 5.81; N=79 reviewers, 49 ideas per condition) but only ~5% of 4000 seeds were non-duplicates.
agent_test: Measure unique-after-dedup yield per token for brainstorm step; dedup and rerank.

claim: LLM outputs are homogeneous: across-model similarity 71-82% (Artificial Hivemind) and ChatGPT brainstorming raises group-level similarity (d=.47), so repeated sampling and persona prompts give less real diversity than they appear to.
agent_test: Embed rival hypotheses and measure pairwise similarity; reject near-duplicates.

claim: Debate with a stronger debater raises judge truthfulness: non-expert LLM judges 76% vs 48% naive; humans 88% vs 60%.
agent_test: Use an independent judge that sees both sides, not the debater.

claim: Multi-agent conversation prompts debias clinical diagnosis: initial diagnosis 0/80 correct, best framework top-2 differential 76% (61/80).
agent_test: Generate a differential before committing; score top-k not top-1.

claim: No direct LLM study of ACH, key-assumptions check or premortem with measured results was found; AI devil's advocate systems (Lee 2025, Chiang 2024) report design or group-decision outcomes only.
agent_test: This is the open gap; run ACH vs plain at equal tokens ourselves.

claim: LLM forecasting: LLM crowd Brier 0.20 vs human crowd 0.19 (no difference); best retrieval system 0.179 vs crowd 0.149.
agent_test: Ensemble of diverse rivals evaluated by Brier.

claim: Anticipatory-reflection devil's advocate for agents: WebArena 23.5% vs LATS 22.7% and Plan+Reflexion 19.8%, 45% fewer plan revisions.
agent_test: Test pre-action failure-imagination at equal steps.

claim: Red teaming by LM generates diverse failures at scale (0.5M zero-shot cases, 3.7% offensive replies), supporting automated adversary generation.
agent_test: Use an adversary generator on the agent's own plan.

claim: Solo Performance Prompting persona collaboration: fixed-persona variants terminate early in many runs (Codenames 37/50 with system message vs 4/50 without), a boundary condition on persona prompts.
agent_test: Check persona prompt does not truncate the run.

claim: Human analysts: ACH raised ratings of cue usefulness (r .68 vs .17, d=1.59) but not accuracy (MAE ACH 0.26 vs control 0.21, p=.14); coherentizing (-35% MAE) plus averaging 50 analysts (-61% MAE, 0.23 to 0.09) gave the real gains, mostly variance reduction.
agent_test: Compare, at equal tokens: plain, rival-list step, and N samples averaged and normalised over rival probabilities; score by MAE or Brier.

claim: Wilcox & Mandel 2024 did not pool effect sizes: 244 hits, 7 papers, 6 experiments, verbal tally, verdict little or no benefit and possible harm. No meta-analytic effect size exists for ACH.
agent_test: Treat ACH benefits as unproven; do not claim a number.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Factored verification works better than joint review: CoVe Wikidata list precision 0.17 to 0.36 (two-step), 0.32 factored; longform FactScore 63.7 to 71.4 with factor+revise. Checking claims independently avoids copying the draft's errors. Closest tested analogue to a key-assumptions check.
agent_test: Arm: assumption check done as separate, independent per-assumption queries vs a joint 'review your answer' prompt; count wrong flips.

claim: Nemeth, Brown & Rogers 2001: an authentic minority beat all three forms of role-played devil's advocate on quantity and quality of solutions; exact means not verified (abstract only). An LLM test of authentic-rival vs assigned-critic prompts does not exist in what we found.
agent_test: Arm: rival must argue its own best conclusion with evidence vs critic assigned to attack the leader.

claim: Words of estimative probability: 7 of 10 LLMs map uncertainty phrases to numbers like humans, but mapping shifts with whether the statement is true (prior-knowledge bias, more than humans). No study tests whether a fixed range table improves LLM calibration.
agent_test: Ask for numbers, or fix a range table and measure Brier with and without it.
